Hi! I’m Milena, a **quantitative social scientist**. I grew up in Brazil and moved to Belgium when I was eighteen, where I spent two years as an au pair, learning Dutch at the KU Leuven. Watching children grow up in a different context than my own made me curious about how the environments we grow up in shape who we become. I have been in the Netherlands for five years now, and am currently based in Leiden.

Through a bachelor’s in Psychology at Maastricht University, I learned to think about behaviour in context. I also discovered a passion for the quantitative side of research, especially the challenge of measuring things that aren’t directly observable, like well-being or social relationships. A master’s in Statistics and Data Science gave me a stronger foundation in statistical modelling, research design, and working with complex data. For my master's thesis at Statistics Netherlands (CBS), I used a whole-population network of the Netherlands to investigate how people's embeddedness in different social domains, such as work, neighbourhood, and household, relates to generalised trust. I enjoy applying quantitative methods to answer relevant social questions, and questioning what the patterns I find actually mean in people’s daily lives.

I am looking to continue working in applied statistics, answering questions about how social contexts shape individual outcomes. Methodologically, I am particularly interested in **measurement and psychometrics**, **multilevel and longitudinal modelling**, and **social network analysis**.

Outside of research, you’ll find me taking care of my tropical plants and having deep discussions about the meaning of life. I love learning about new cultures, exploring different perspectives, watching art house films, and going down rabbit holes about whatever has caught my attention lately. Whenever I get the chance, I also like to scuba dive.
